text:
Maria: Quick sketch — cold-starts from safetensors shards are causing 700–1500ms latency spikes for our large LMs when a new model hotpath hits. Current warmup pulls entire shard files which is slow. Thinking about a "partial rehydration" path: prefetch a small, prioritized set of tensors (big matrices, attention KV, LN params), and lazily hydrate small ones. Thoughts? :thinking:
Alex: Love it. How do you pick priorities? by tensor size or by usage heatmap?
Maria: initial heuristic: size + layer role (attention/query/key/value, kv-cache). But we could feed runtime telemetry (recent prompts -> which layers get hit early) to compute a token-heat priority.
Sam: tradeoff: adding richer tensor index and hints increases manifest overhead and complexity for transports (S3/GCS). We should quantify index size vs savings. Could be worth it if index compresses well.
Jing: API idea — add an optional prefetch hint block to the safetensors manifest. Example (proto):
```json
{
  "manifest_version": 2,
  "prefetch_hints": ["attn_qkv","ln_scale","lm_head"],
  "tensor_index": {"layer_0.attn.qkv": [12345, 98765], "layer_0.ln.scale": [11111,512]}
}
```
This keeps runtime decision local: weightsource reads index and issues range requests for critical tensors.
Alex: Nice. We should also surface a runtime API: WeightSource.open(prefetch_hints=[...], max_bytes=...) so downstream services can opt in.
Taylor: Another pattern: bundle a small "hot-header" file with the top ~5% of tensors (by priority) to avoid many small range requests on systems that have poor range efficiency. Bundles are optional but can be generated as a build optimization.
Sam: Concern: on Dedicated/private deployments, generating bundles could increase storage variants we need to track. Maybe we make bundling a build-time toggle in the model registry.
Maria: Good point. Proposal: two-tier metadata: lightweight tensor_index (required) + optional prefetch_manifest and optional hot-header bundle. Runtime uses index-first path and falls back to hot-header when available.
runtime-bot: Deploy metric: model-load.cold_start.ms median=720, p95=1450 since last rollout. Prefetch path expected to reduce p95 by ~30–60% in sim.
Jing: Also consider a small, versioned transport shim: index-first URLs -> return 206 byte ranges. If transport doesn't support ranges, fallback to whole-file fetch or hot-header.
Alex: Implementation plan: 1) add index schema v2, 2) extend model-publish to optionally emit hot-header, 3) WeightSource API for prefetch hints, 4) telemetry hooks for token-heat feedback.
Taylor: Quick perf microbenchmark suggestion: simulate 1000 cold starts with and without prefetch on S3 with 200ms latency and 5ms per-range overhead. Measure end-to-end 1st-token latency.
Maria: Agree. I'll prototype a minimal shim that: reads tensor_index, issues range GETs for top-N, then returns early while streaming the rest. If range-overhead kills us, fallback to header-bundle.
Sam: +1. Also add a flag to the loader to force eager full-load for small models to avoid complexity.
Maria: Action items: Maria -> prototype shim and perf script (this week). Jing -> draft manifest schema (v2) and compatibility notes. Alex/Taylor -> help perf experiments. Sam -> list infra implications for registry and storage variants. We'll reconvene Fri. :thumbsup:
